newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Tractebel to manage Kazakhstan's gas pipelines.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel to manage Kazakhstan's gas pipelines.

text.p: Belgium's Tractebel S.A. has won a repeat tender for the right to manage Kazakhstan's gas pipeline network for 15 years in a deal worth $630 million, the government said on Monday.

"We decided on Saturday that Tractebel was the winner of the tender for the western and southern (gas) pipeline systems," Dyusenbai Duysenov, Kazakhstan's deputy prime minister in charge of industry, told a news conference.

Under the deal, Tractebel will manage the republic's 9,000 km (6,000 mile) gas pipeline network for 15 years, with an option to renew for another five years, in which the transport of 65 billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas is seen annually.
Duysenov said Tractebel would invest about $600 million in the network and would pay the Kazakh government, anxious for cash to tackle unpaid wages and pensions, a $30 million bonus.

Tractebel, which will pay the government a royalty of two percent on gas volumes and pay the government 10-40 percent of its profits, beat Argentina's Bridas Energy Corp and a consortium comprising U.S. Enron Corp and Gaz de France in the tender.

The western Batystransgaz network, which carries Turkmen gas to Russia and Europe, transports about 60 billion bcm of gas and is the most profitable. Tractebel has said it will build a 156 km gas pipeline to bypass neighbour Kyrgyzstan for the delivery of Uzbek gas to southern Kazakhstan via its Alaugaz network.
